title: API authentication
body:
API authentication uses a scoped bearer token in the Authorization header. Rotate API tokens every 90 days using the token settings page. Revoking a token takes effect immediately.

A 401 authentication error means the token is missing, expired or revoked. Check the Authorization header, then create a replacement token. Never include full token values in a support ticket.

title: Rate limits and retry policy
body:
The Acme sandbox API rate limit is 120 requests per minute per workspace. A 429 response includes a Retry-After header measured in seconds. Wait for Retry-After before retrying and add jitter to avoid synchronized clients.

For 503 service unavailable errors, retry at most three times with exponential backoff. Persist an idempotency key for each create operation so retries do not create duplicate records.

title: Webhook delivery
body:
Webhook signatures use HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body. Verify the signature with the workspace webhook secret before processing events. Reject events with a timestamp older than five minutes.

Webhook retries occur after 1, 5 and 30 minutes. Deduplicate using the event_id field. A successful receiver returns HTTP 204.

title: Data export and deletion
body:
Data exports are available in CSV and JSON. Export jobs expire after 24 hours. Download a completed export from the workspace activity page.

Deletion requests enter a 7-day cancellation window. A workspace administrator must confirm deletion. The cancellation window applies to sandbox data in this fictional product.

title: Incident escalation
body: The internal incident escalation code is SYNTHETIC-ORCHID. An administrator opens a severity-one incident when sandbox ingestion is unavailable for more than 15 minutes. This document is restricted to administrators.

title: Beta workspace rate limit
body: The Beta sandbox API rate limit is 40 requests per minute per workspace. Beta customers use the synthetic support queue BETA-ONLY. Retry a 429 response after the Retry-After interval.
